next_step: Closed-lost to AWS managed endpoints — pause; follow-up 2026-05 for migration opportunity
notes:
Summary: Closed-lost to AWS managed endpoints (SageMaker / Bedrock) after procurement review. Solaris decided to standardize on their existing AWS contracts and consolidated billing. Key factors: lower integration lift, enterprise discount, single-vendor support, and perceived faster time-to-production.

Deal history / timeline:
- 2025-09-02: Lead created after inbound from webinar (personalization @ scale).
- 2025-10-20: Intro call (AE Maya) — Solaris product + infra overview; interest: chat for customer support, embeddings for search, reranking in recommendation engine.
- 2025-11-05: Technical deep-dive with SE Daniel — discussed latency SLOs (p95 < 120ms for short chat turns), throughput target ~200 reqs/s, burst to 1k. Talked about KV cache, batching.
- 2026-01-06: POC kicked off (2-week) using Redwood Dedicated trial cluster; objective: end-to-end latency/cost comparison vs internal prototype.
- 2026-01-20: Mid-POC check — Redwood met latency targets on 2x A100 nodes; cost per 1M tokens projected in mid-range vs hyperscaler.
- 2026-02-11: Procurement + security review (Fireflies meeting ff_20260211_solaris_poc_review). CTO quote: "We don't want to operate another vendor — pressing for fewer vendors and less ops overhead."
- 2026-02-14: Final decision: procurement chooses AWS managed endpoints to keep everything under current cloud agreement and use existing cloud-native IAM/KMS flows.

Why we lost:
- Hyperscaler advantage: Solaris already on AWS, they prioritized single-vendor consolidation and preferred SageMaker/Bedrock managed endpoints with native Lake and IAM integration.
- Integration friction: Procurement saw Redwood as "another vendor to onboard" despite strong technical fit.
- Pricing & discounts: AWS committed enterprise credits and a pricing pilot that lowered the near-term cost delta.
- Internal champion: Product lead who pushed for Redwood accepted a sideways compromise; no executive escalation.

Technical notes captured during POC:
- Redwood Dedicated latency: p95 ~95ms on test workload (short chat prompts), throughput sustained ~220 reqs/s with batching.
- Feature fit: Redwood supports required features (prefix caching, canary rollouts, KV cache). Solaris liked model-routing ideas but prioritized simpler ops.
- Security: Redwood offered KMS integration + VPC private endpoints; procurement flagged perceived extra configurations vs AWS-managed KMS and centralized billing.

Follow-up plan (recommendation):
- Mark as closed-lost; log win reasons for AWS in Deal Desk.
- Send a short "congrats & keep in touch" note + 2-page competitive teardown comparing Redwood vs SageMaker/Bedrock (focus: TCO at 12/24 months, migration costs, quality/regression monitoring advantages).
- Re-engage after 90 days to offer a migration-in option and an independent cost/latency audit (offer limited free audit for migration opportunities).

- Security QA summary: /security/solarisdw/security-qa-2026-01.pdf
- Support ticket about POC model failure: INF-4127

Sales notes / shorthand:

- SE: Daniel — capture Redwood performance graphs and one-pager to include in competitive teardown.
